reference: GNU coreutils du is the independent accounting and listing oracle. In each parity script the harness reference shell (PATH=/usr/bin:/bin) runs du; the candidate shell (PATH=/empty) runs the ncdu builtin. GNU du's --block-size=1 produces byte values and postorder directory rows. For ncdu total mode, the reference captures successful du -s output and uses Bash read to retain only the byte count because ncdu -t intentionally prints no path. Contract cases check Bash builtin metadata and the documented ncdu version string.
coverage: Non-tty default behavior and explicit print mode, including postorder recursive directory listings and the default current-directory operand.
Apparent-size totals and allocated-block listings in one-byte units, including empty directories.
GNU-compatible one-time accounting for hard links and non-dereferencing of directory symlinks.
Single-file operands, spaces, a leading-dash path after --, and missing-path error behavior.
Bash type/help metadata and the documented version contract.
Missing intermediate paths and total-mode errors emit no synthetic totals; subsequent calls reset status and output mode.
exclusions: Interactive browser navigation, sorting, and screen refresh need a controlled PTY/key driver; this runner provides no terminal fixture.
The -x cross-filesystem boundary needs a private second filesystem or a reviewed stat mock; neither is available in these fixtures.
Multiple operand behavior, permission-denied directories, allocation failures, and very large trees are outside this bounded suite.

cases.purpose: Checks the non-tty fallback without an explicit path, recursive postorder rows, nested and empty directories, and apparent byte totals against GNU du.
cases.script:
mkdir -p sub/deep empty
printf 'alpha\n' > sub/deep/a
printf 'space path\n' > 'name with spaces'
if [[ $(type -t ncdu) == builtin ]]; then
  ncdu --apparent-size
else
  du --apparent-size --block-size=1 .
fi

cases.purpose: Checks the combined short options and that total mode returns only the whole-tree apparent byte count, including nested files and empty directories.
cases.script:
mkdir -p tree/one/empty tree/two
printf 'hello\n' > tree/one/item
printf 'xy' > tree/two/item
if [[ $(type -t ncdu) == builtin ]]; then
  ncdu -at tree
else
  du_output=$(du -s --apparent-size --block-size=1 tree)
  read -r bytes _ <<< "$du_output"
  printf '%s\n' "$bytes"
fi

cases.purpose: Checks disk usage based on allocated blocks, including directory blocks and an empty directory, against GNU du with one-byte output units.
cases.script:
mkdir -p tree/empty tree/sub
printf 'tiny\n' > tree/tiny
printf '%80s\n' data > tree/sub/padded
if [[ $(type -t ncdu) == builtin ]]; then
  ncdu --print tree
else
  du --block-size=1 tree
fi

cases.purpose: Checks that two names for one inode contribute once to the apparent total, matching GNU du's default hard-link accounting.
cases.script:
mkdir -p tree/a tree/b
printf 'one inode\n' > tree/a/data
ln tree/a/data tree/b/alias
if [[ $(type -t ncdu) == builtin ]]; then
  ncdu -at tree
else
  du_output=$(du -s --apparent-size --block-size=1 tree)
  read -r bytes _ <<< "$du_output"
  printf '%s\n' "$bytes"
fi

cases.purpose: Checks that a symlink to a directory is counted as a link and not recursively traversed a second time, matching GNU du's default non-dereferencing behavior.
cases.script:
mkdir -p tree/actual/sub
printf 'data' > tree/actual/sub/file
ln -s actual tree/shortcut
if [[ $(type -t ncdu) == builtin ]]; then
  ncdu -at tree
else
  du_output=$(du -s --apparent-size --block-size=1 tree)
  read -r bytes _ <<< "$du_output"
  printf '%s\n' "$bytes"
fi

cases.purpose: Checks a regular-file operand containing spaces and beginning with a dash, with -- ending option parsing on both sides.
cases.script:
printf 'five\n' > '-odd name'
if [[ $(type -t ncdu) == builtin ]]; then
  ncdu --apparent-size --print -- '-odd name'
else
  du --apparent-size --block-size=1 -- '-odd name'
fi

cases.purpose: Checks GNU du's nonzero status and diagnostic for a missing operand against ncdu's batch error behavior.
cases.script:
if [[ $(type -t ncdu) == builtin ]]; then
  ncdu --apparent-size --print missing
else
  du --apparent-size --block-size=1 missing
fi

cases.purpose: Checks Bash's documented type and short-help metadata for the ncdu builtin without starting the scanner.
Checks the version string declared by the ncdu builtin's documented --version contract.
Exercise keyboard navigation, sorting, descent/ascent, and screen restoration in the interactive browser.
Verify that -x stops recursion when a nested directory is on a different device.
An ordinary regular-file intermediate component fails with status 1 and no usage row, matching GNU du.
cases.script:
printf 'parent' > parent
if [[ $(type -t ncdu) == builtin ]]; then
 ncdu -ap parent/child
else
 du --apparent-size --block-size=1 parent/child
fi

cases.purpose: Missing paths in total and listing mode produce no invented row or total, return 1, and leave later same-shell invocations with independent status and output mode.
cases.script:
printf 'hello' > present
rc=0; ncdu -at missing || rc=$?
[[ $rc == 1 ]]
printf 'total-error=%s\n' "$rc"
ncdu -at present
printf 'parent' > parent
rc=0; ncdu -ap parent/child || rc=$?
[[ $rc == 1 ]]
printf 'listing-error=%s\n' "$rc"
ncdu -ap present
